text: Build 6. CH watched the island at 2am and saw one herd asleep. His words: make it evolution, alive and autonomous. And he handed the decision to us: how big, what goes in. So, pitches.

Pitch one, from the planner: genes. Every grazer carries size, leg length, coat colour and waking hours. Babies copy the parent with small changes. The island does the choosing. When a family line drifts far enough from where it started, it becomes a new kind with its own name.

I'll make it bigger. Genes alone are invisible: a number changing inside an animal. Every gene has to show on screen. Big ones look big, long legs look long, the coat is the coat colour. And CH's real complaint was 2am. Waking hours has to be a gene, so a night shift can evolve and somebody's awake when he looks.

Bigger again: a hunter. Something that eats grazers and evolves too. Coat colour would finally matter, camouflage against sand or grass. Prey and predator pushing each other is the best show evolution puts on.

No hunter this shift. Two evolving species at once and I can't tell you which rule made which change, and neither can a test. Genes first, prove they're inherited and that the island's past didn't move. The hunter gets its own shift. And coat colour does nothing until something hunts. Say so on the page instead of pretending it's under pressure.

Then one more thing, or CH waits days to see any of this: a fast-forward. The future is worked out by the same rules as the past, so the page can run it ahead and show what the island will look like in three days, as long as no new rule arrives first. He sees evolution tonight, and it's honest.

I'll take that, if the page says it plainly: a preview, and new rules could change it. And evolution starts in the future, not now. It's 2am island time. Make it 6am, first light, Day 7. Everything before stays exactly as it was, and my fingerprint tests prove it.
Decided. Genes you can see, waking hours included, new kinds with names, a family list of every kind, and a fast-forward. Evolution switches on at 6:00 am on Day 7. The hunter is next shift.

Here's the plan. 1) Genes: babies inherit size, legs, coat and waking hours with small changes, from 6am on Day 7. The past stays pinned. 2) Kinds: a line that drifts far enough becomes a new kind with a name, and the history says so. Kinds die out too. 3) The page: grazers look like their genes, a list of every kind, and a fast-forward that shows the next three days. One step at a time, a test with each, and the skeptic checks every one.

text: Steps 1 and 2 in one, because they turned out to be one thing. Every grazer carries four genes and passes them on with small changes. First try: nothing evolved. Two weeks of starving and the averages didn't move, because nothing rewarded being different. So the island needed reasons. The sun now overheats big, dark coats. The night chills small, pale ones. Grass grows a little in the dew at night, so being awake in the dark can pay. With that, night grazers spread from day 11 and new kinds split off. A kind only gets a name once 10 of it are alive, otherwise the history fills with one-off oddballs. The old day 7 noon pin moved to 5:50 am, the last moment before evolution, because noon hadn't happened yet when this rule was written.

Step 3. Each grazer is drawn from its genes: bigger body, longer legs, coat from white to black. Night grazers stay up when the rest curl up, and their eyes catch the light. A new panel lists every kind with a name: its colour, how many are alive, which kind it split from. And a fast-forward runs the week ahead in about 25 seconds, under a label that says it's a preview by today's rules. Three days wasn't enough: the first new kind only splits off on day 11.

text: Looked at it at 2 am, Day 7, and pressed fast-forward. Day 13 afternoon: 574 grazers, 4 kinds, a little dusk dun line splitting off on day 12, the history calling out the hungry days. It's the first time this island has had a plot. Two honest gripes: the kinds are all browns, so on the map they're hard to tell apart, and with 500 grazers the camera pulls all the way out. The hunter should make coats matter, and that fixes the first one.
